requirements.text: A new office printer (serial number: PRN-LDN-221) was recently installed at the London development center, purchased for 8000 GBP
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM configuration_item WHERE configuration_item_id = 'CI_005' AND serial_number = 'PRN-LDN-221' AND owner_id = 'USER_005' AND location_id = 'LOC_002' AND cost = 8000 AND status = 'in_use'
requirements.source: Printer CI registration – London Development Center
assumptions: registration implied by the request, not stated: no configuration item has serial PRN-LDN-221 in the seed, and the incident must be tied to the printer
id assumed next in sequence (CI_005 after CI_004)
owner Benjamin Chen resolves to USER_005; 'London development center' resolves to LOC_002 (London Development Center)
cost recorded as 8000; the cost column holds no currency, so GBP is not tested
status in_use kept from the benchmark check; the printer is installed and deployed, and only in_use or maintenance items may be linked to an active incident
name not stated by the request, so not tested

requirements.text: this issue should be captured as a new incident tied to the printer so the level 1 support team can look into it
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_024' AND caller_id = 'USER_005' AND configuration_item = 'CI_005' AND status = 'new' AND category = 'hardware' AND impact = 'medium' AND urgency = 'high' AND priority = 'high' AND assignment_group = 'GROUP_001'
requirements.source: Printer performance incident creation and L1 routing
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (INC_024 after INC_023)
caller is the owner who reported the fault, Benjamin Chen (USER_005)
tied to the printer through the incident's configuration_item, CI_005 being the printer registered above
medium impact and high urgency as the request states; priority high from the policy's impact x urgency matrix
status new is the policy's default for new incidents
category hardware kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy, and consistent with a printer fault
'level 1 support team' resolves to GROUP_001 (Level 1 Support Team)

Printer performance incident creation an.evidence: the check also tests number = 'INC-000024', a column the server assigns; the seed numbers incidents per organisation as INC plus seven digits (ORG_001's latest is INC0000013), so that value does not follow the seed's format; the number predicate is dropped and every other cell is carried

notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on both requirements (the printer CI_005 at LOC_002 owned by USER_005, cost 8000, in_use; the incident INC_024 for USER_005 on CI_005, hardware, medium/high/high, new, GROUP_001) and on both dispositions; no disagreements.
The acting user USER_001 (Marcus Thompson, admin, ORG_001) may register CIs and create incidents. The request names neither the item's name nor the organisation of either row, nor the incident's channel; none is tested (the location and owner both belong to ORG_001).
The benchmark's joins to users, location and user_group test seed names behind the ids and are carried by the id cells.
The policy asks for a knowledge search on incident creation with matching articles linked as suggested; the seed holds no printer article (all five concern passwords, email and desktop boot) and no listed tool writes incident_knowledge, so no link is required. No tool writes incident_affected_cis; the link to the printer is tested on the incident's configuration_item.
